title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page. It is a typed page, p. 123 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 I (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §10.2). It apparently sits in the dossier because Grothendieck reused old SGA 7 typescript sheets as paper for his 1975-76 notes on divided-power de Rham complexes. The neighbouring manuscript pages on generalized de Rham functors are unrelated in content.

The mathematics, in modern terms:
- Setting: K is the fraction field of a henselian discrete valuation ring with base S. A_K and \bar A_K are abelian varieties over K with semistable reduction.
- Input: ξ is a biextension of (A_K, \bar A_K) by G_m. Equivalently, it is a homomorphism \bar A_K → A'_K into the dual abelian variety.
- Step 1: by the Néron mapping property this homomorphism extends to the Néron models. It then restricts to a homomorphism between the maximal tori of the identity components of the special fibres.
- Step 2: contravariance of character groups gives (10.2.6), ξ_t : \bar M → M'. Here M and M' are the twisted constant groups (character groups of the toric parts) of A and A', and \bar M is the analogous group for \bar A.
- Step 3: composing with the monodromy pairing φ^t : M ⊗ M' → Z (tensored to Z_ℓ) gives (10.2.7), φ^t_ξ(x,y) = φ^t(x, ξ_t(y)), a pairing M_ℓ ⊗ \bar M_ℓ → Z_ℓ.
- Functoriality: M is covariant in A_K under semistable reduction, so the formation of these pairings is compatible with pullback of biextensions.
- For ξ the canonical Weil (Poincaré) biextension of (A_K, A'_K), the construction recovers the monodromy pairing (9.2.1).
- Symmetry: the transposed biextension ^sξ is a biextension of (\bar A_K, A_K). Its pairing satisfies (10.2.8), φ^t_{^sξ} = φ^t_ξ ∘ s.
- Grothendieck contrasts this symmetry with the antisymmetry of the Weil pairing on Tate modules in VIII 2.2.11.

The point of the passage is to recast the symmetry of the monodromy pairing (proved in SGA 7 IX via the biextension formalism) in a form functorial in arbitrary biextensions. Applied to the biextension coming from a polarization, it gives the symmetric pairing on the character group that underlies Raynaud and Mumford degenerations.
errors: In (10.2.7) the defining formula is written φ^t(x,y) = φ^t(x, ξ_t(y)). The left-hand side should be φ^t_ξ(x,y); this is a notational slip in the typescript, not a mathematical error.
No mathematical errors detected. The construction and the symmetry statement match the published SGA 7 IX §10.

ideas.what: Pairing on character groups of the toric parts induced by an arbitrary biextension of semistable abelian varieties, obtained by composing with the monodromy pairing
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck monodromy pairing (functorial version for biextensions/homomorphisms to the dual)

ideas.what: Symmetry relation φ_{^sξ} = φ_ξ ∘ s, contrasted with the antisymmetry of the Weil pairing (VIII 2.2.11)
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, (10.2.8); compare Exp. VIII 2.2.11

ideas.what: Covariant functoriality of the twisted constant character group M in A_K under semistable reduction, and compatibility of the pairings with pullback of biextensions
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of the character group of the toric part of the Néron model

missed.claim: This is a typed page of the published SGA 7 IX, not new material. Its presence in cote 136 indicates that the 1975-76 divided-power de Rham notes were written on the backs of discarded SGA 7 typescript. This is relevant for dating and for archival description; it has no mathematical novelty.
missed.quote: - 123 - IX ... On comparera cette relation à la relation d'antisymétrie de VIII 2.2.11.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only archival: the reverse of each sheet in cote 136 should be cross-checked against SGA 7, so that typescript pages are not catalogued as unpublished notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is verbatim from the published SGA 7 I, Exposé IX §10.2 (monodromy pairing for biextensions and its symmetry). Nothing here is unpublished or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: The page is a typescript (SGA 7 IX, p. 123), not a manuscript. The archive stamp '441' and the '111' in the margin are archival numbering.
In (10.2.7) the M's are underlined in the typescript: \underline{M}_ℓ ⊗ \overline{\underline{M}}_ℓ → Z_ℓ. The right-hand formula reads φ^t(x,y) = φ^t(x, ξ_t(y)) as typed.
'à réduction semi-stable variable' is as typed. The transcription 'a réduction' should read 'à réduction'.
